passages.title: Text A
text: My name is Elif, and I've worked as a nurse since 2015.
I used to work in a small clinic in my hometown, but three years ago I moved to a bigger hospital in Istanbul, where I've been ever since.

The job I do now is completely different from the one I used to have — back then, I mostly saw patients with minor problems, but now I work in the emergency department, which is much more stressful but also more rewarding.
If I hadn't moved cities, I probably wouldn't have met my husband, who is a doctor at the same hospital.
We met on my very first day, when I got completely lost in the building and he showed me the way to the right department.
Since then, a lot has changed in our lives: we got married last year, and we've just bought a small flat near the hospital.
The flat was built in the 1960s, so it needed a lot of work before we could move in — the kitchen, for example, had to be completely rebuilt.
My colleague, who has been a nurse for over twenty years, always says that the best thing about this job is the people you meet, not the money.
I completely agree with her.
If I were braver, I'd probably apply for a senior position next year, but for now, I'm happy just learning as much as I can from the more experienced staff around me.

questions.prompt: Elif has worked as a nurse since 2015.
She still works in the small clinic in her hometown.
Elif met her husband on her first day at the new hospital.
The flat they bought didn't need any work.
Why hasn't Elif applied for a senior position yet?
options: She wants to learn more from experienced staff first

passages.title: Text B
text: Last summer, my friend Tomasz and I decided to cycle from Warsaw to the Baltic coast, something neither of us had ever done before.
We'd been planning the trip for months, and we were both really excited when the day finally came.
The first two days went smoothly — the roads were quieter than we'd expected, and the weather was much better than the forecast had predicted.
On the third day, though, everything went wrong.
We were cycling through a forest when it suddenly started raining heavily, and within minutes we were both soaked.
While we were looking for somewhere to shelter, Tomasz's bike got a flat tyre, and neither of us had brought the right tools to fix it.
We had to push our bikes for almost five kilometres until we found a small village, where a very kind man let us stay in his garage for the night.
The next morning, he even helped us repair the tyre before we left.
If that hadn't happened, I don't think we would have finished the trip at all — we were both ready to give up.
In the end, we reached the coast four days later than planned, but it didn't matter.
I've never felt as proud of anything as I did standing on that beach, completely exhausted but happy.
We've already started talking about our next trip, although this time we've agreed to check the weather forecast a bit more carefully, and to bring some proper tools with us.

questions.prompt: Tomasz and the narrator had cycled this route before.
The weather was worse than the forecast had predicted at the start of the trip.
A stranger let them stay in his garage.
They finished the trip exactly on the day they had planned.
What have they agreed to do differently next time?
options: Check the weather forecast more carefully and bring proper tools

lines.t: Hi, I'm calling about the MovNat training course in November.
OK, great. Are you interested in coming on the course?
Yes, I am, but I've just got a few questions I'd like to ask. Do you need to have a good level of fitness?
No, no. The course is for anybody. It doesn't matter how fit you are. When you arrive, the instructor will check your fitness level.
Right. And what will happen if it rains or snows? Will you cancel it, or will it be indoors?
No. The course will take place outside, whatever the weather.
OK. So is it necessary to book a place, or would it be alright to just turn up?
No, you'll definitely need to reserve a place before you come. There are only two or three places left in November.
I just need to check I can make those dates. Then I'll call and book.

questions.prompt: Does the caller need to be very fit to join the course?
options: No, the course is for anybody

questions.prompt: What happens to the course if it rains or snows?
Why does the caller decide not to book immediately?
options: She needs to check her dates first
She doesn't want to go anymore

grammar.en: Go back through the grammar stage of Lessons 1–36 — focus especially on Present Perfect vs Past Simple, the two conditionals, the passive, and used to.
grammar.ru: Вернитесь к грамматике уроков 1–36 — особенно Present Perfect и Past Simple, два типа условных предложений, пассив и used to.
grammar.kk: 1–36-сабақтардың грамматикасына оралыңыз — әсіресе Present Perfect пен Past Simple, шартты сөйлемдердің екі түрі, ырықсыз етіс және used to.

vocabulary.en: Revisit the flashcards across units — character, money, food and job-application vocabulary come up again and again.
vocabulary.ru: Повторите карточки по всем юнитам — характер, деньги, еда и лексика для устройства на работу встречаются снова и снова.

reading.en: Re-read the reading-led lessons (they're written specially for this course, not from the coursebook), and practise picking out the key fact rather than every word.
reading.ru: Перечитайте уроки с упором на чтение (тексты написаны специально для курса, в учебнике их нет) и тренируйтесь находить главный факт, а не переводить каждое слово.
reading.kk: Оқылымға арналған сабақтарды қайта оқыңыз (мәтіндер осы курсқа арнайы жазылған, оқулықта жоқ) және әр сөзді емес, негізгі фактіні табуға жаттығыңыз.
